name: openscreen-demo
cost: Free (MIT). OpenScreen is free for personal and commercial use
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other MCP clients. macOS, Windows and Linux
short: Has your agent record, edit and export a demo video of a feature with OpenScreen, then attach it to a pull request or draft an X post.
what: OpenScreen is a free desktop app for recording your screen and turning it into polished demos. This AI skill drives it through its MCP tools: it writes a storyboard, records the app window, cuts dead time, adds zooms and callouts, exports an MP4 and checks it frame by frame. A pull request video runs 10 to 30 seconds. A launch demo runs 20 to 60 seconds and comes with a drafted post for X.
who: Developers who want a short video on their pull requests or a launch clip without editing it by hand. You need a desktop session the app can record, so it won't work from a remote shell.
needs: The OpenScreen app: macOS 13 or newer, Windows 10 version 1903 or newer, or Linux with xdg-desktop-portal and PipeWire
8 GB of RAM at least, 16 GB recommended
A coding agent that supports MCP servers
For pull request videos: `gh` 2.99.0 or newer and push access to the repo

steps.title: Install OpenScreen
steps.text: On Windows, the Microsoft Store is the recommended route. On macOS, download the `.dmg` from the Releases page and drag it to Applications. Linux has `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.pacman` and AppImage packages.

steps.title: Grant permissions on a Mac
steps.text: In System Settings, Privacy & Security, give OpenScreen Screen Recording and Accessibility. Recording won't start without both.

steps.title: Connect the MCP server
steps.text: `<executable>` is the app's executable on your system. On macOS it is `/Applications/Openscreen.app/Contents/MacOS/Openscreen`. The SKILL.md lists the Windows and Linux paths.

steps.title: Start a new session and ask
steps.text: The agent loads MCP servers when a session starts, so open a new one before you ask for a video.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Add a video of this change to the PR.

watch: If OpenScreen is missing, the skill offers to install the latest release and does it only once you agree.
Nothing is posted to X without your explicit yes.
Keep secrets, customer data and personal notifications off screen. The skill blurs private details it spots, but check the frames.
GitHub accepts videos up to 10 MB on a free plan and 100 MB on a paid one.
When connected to the server inside the app, you must turn on MCP edits under AI settings before it can record or export.
The Windows `.exe` from Releases isn't code-signed, so SmartScreen warns. The Store version installs without a warning.
OpenScreen is under active development, so expect rough edges and breaking changes.
